garment_activity_ratings.activity_notes: Optimized for resort skiing. Insulation too warm for sustained uphill. Excellent for cold chairlift days.
Active layer for variable conditions. Excellent wind/abrasion resistance. Best layered over another fleece in cold.
Insulated ski bibs with H2No waterproofing. Excellent for resort and backcountry descents. Thigh vents for temperature regulation.
Insulated ski jacket with H2No waterproofing. 60g insulation throughout. Helmet-compatible hood. Best for resort skiing.
Ultralight active insulation vest. FullRange insulation is highly breathable. Perfect for high-output activities in cold.
PlumaFill synthetic insulation mimics down. Warm, packable, performs wet. Good belay jacket or cold weather midlayer.
Ultralight PlumaFill insulation. Extremely packable. Best warmth-to-weight ratio in synthetic. Good for active cold or emergency warmth.
Ultralight wind shell. Packs into own pocket. Essential for transitions and summits. Not waterproof but DWR handles light precip.
Polartec Power Grid fleece pants. Excellent breathability for high-output activities. Works as midlayer or standalone in mild cold.
Budget lightweight synthetic base layer. Good moisture wicking for the price. Best for mild cold or high output.
Budget lightweight synthetic base layer bottom. Thin and breathable. Best for mild cold or high output.
Budget midweight synthetic base layer bottom. Brushed interior for warmth. Good value for cold weather.
Coreloft synthetic in core, Polartec fleece in arms. Versatile active insulation. Industry benchmark for midlayer/belay jacket.
Ultralight emergency shell. Wets out in sustained rain. Poor breathability but excellent packability.
Lightweight softshell with excellent stretch and breathability. Wind resistant face. Ideal for high-output aerobic activities.
Lightweight stretchy softshell pants. Wind resistant, breathable. Great for hiking, XC skiing, casual use.
LIFA polypropylene wicks faster than any other fiber. Excellent for high-output cold weather. Too thin for static cold.
Lightweight LIFA base layer bottom. Excellent moisture management for high output. Pair with shell for wind protection.
80g/60g body-mapped PrimaLoft. H2Flow ventilation. RECCO rescue. Life Pocket+ keeps phone warm. Premium resort ski jacket.
PFC-free LIFA Infinity Pro membrane. 80g recycled PrimaLoft Black Eco. H2Flow ventilation. Premium eco-focused flagship.
Ultralight packable midlayer. Best for active use and transitions. Not warm enough for static cold.
Resort ski jacket. Waterproof warmth for lifts and groomers. Too warm/heavy for touring.
Versatile active insulated shell. Good for variable conditions hiking/touring. Stretch allows full mobility.
Casual/lifestyle puffer. Water-resistant not waterproof. Good value option for light activity.
Dual-layer fabric: brushed grid interior traps air, smooth exterior. 4-way stretch. Good for high activity in cold.
Brushed grid interior, smooth exterior. 4-way stretch. Midweight protection for cold/high activity.
Classic fleece midlayer. Good breathability and warmth. Relaxed fit works well as casual or technical layer.
Synthetic insulated jacket with water-resistant shell. Omni-Heat reflective lining. Good value resort option.
Synthetic insulated vest with Omni-Heat. Good core warmth without restricting arms. Versatile layering piece.
3-in-1 interchange system with waterproof shell and insulated liner. Heavy but versatile. Best for resort skiing in cold.
Lightweight synthetic base layer with Omni-Wick moisture management. Good value option for moderate cold.
Midweight stretch base layer bottom with Omni-Heat. 4-way stretch for mobility. Good value cold weather option.
Premium resort ski jacket. Waterproof with PrimaLoft insulation. Built for chairlift-to-groomer skiing in cold conditions.
Mid-range resort ski jacket. Waterproof with synthetic insulation. Lighter than Leader for milder conditions.
Performance synthetic base layer. T-Hot technology for warmth. 4-way stretch with flatlock seams.
Performance synthetic base layer bottom. T-Hot technology. 4-way stretch with flatlock seams.
Premium Gore-Tex ski pant. Fully waterproof/windproof shell. Thigh vents for temperature regulation. Pair with base/mid layers for warmth.
Heavy-duty winter parka with 700-fill down. Urban/casual focus. Too warm for most active skiing but excellent for extreme cold standby.
Budget-friendly insulated resort ski pant. Omni-Heat reflective lining with 60g synthetic insulation. Too warm for high-output activities.
Premium Gore-Tex Pro ePE shell pant. Full weather protection with side vents. Pairs with base layers for temperature tuning.
Warm insulated resort ski jacket. VerticalX Eco 80g body / 60g sleeves. Too warm for touring uphill but excellent for chairlift days.
Pertex Shield 3L shell jacket. Lighter and more breathable than Gore-Tex Pro at a lower price point. Excellent layering piece.
Pertex Shield 3L shell bib. 420D scuff guards at cuffs. Bib design adds core warmth and snow protection. Pairs with base layers for flexibility.
Merino exterior with LIFA wicking interior. Best of both worlds: warmth + moisture management. Great for resort skiing.
Merino/LIFA midweight base layer bottom. Good warmth with excellent wicking. Ideal under ski pants in cold conditions.
Polartec Thermal Pro fleece. Warm and pill-resistant. Good midlayer under shell for resort skiing or standalone in mild cold.
40g PrimaLoft Gold Active+. 4-way stretch with fleece side panels. Excellent for ski touring and high-output backcountry use.
80g PrimaLoft Gold Active+. Warmer sibling of the Light version. Good belay jacket or cold weather midlayer with stretch.
3L Helly Tech Pro shell. RECCO rescue system. Life Pocket keeps phone warm. Pair with insulation for cold days.
3L stretch shell with RECCO. Heavier but more durable than Sogn. PFC-free DWR. Good for resort and backcountry descents.
3L shell bib with stretch back panel. Thigh vents and adjustable suspenders. Pair with base/mid layers for warmth.
Body-mapped PrimaLoft 60g/40g insulation. Mechanical stretch. Inner thigh vents. Reinforced scuff guards. Best-selling HH ski pant.
Wind protection for high-output activities. Not warm enough for lifts or descents.
Polartec Power Grid fleece. Industry standard for active insulation. Excellent breathability with offset seams for comfort under pack straps.
Budget midweight synthetic base layer. Brushed interior traps warmth. Good value for cold weather activities.
Polartec Power Grid. Open grid pattern for warmth/breathability. 22" inseam (boot-length) for ski/snowboard.
Midweight base layer with hollow-core Capilene fabric. Excellent moisture wicking for high-output activities.
